blogs.title: Meet BLT: The Tokenizer-Free Language Model That Thinks in Patches
blogs.description: An approachable intro to Byte Latent Transformer (BLT). Explain how it learns directly from bytes, groups them into dynamic patches based on information density, and reaches Llama-3-level quality with up to 50% lower inference compute plus improved robustness.

blogs.title: Entropy Patching, Explained in Plain English
blogs.description: Demystify how BLT decides where one patch ends and the next begins. Use simple examples to show what entropy (uncertainty) means, why the first character of a word is harder to predict than the rest, and how BLT’s thresholds create smart, context-aware patch boundaries.

blogs.title: Under the Hood of BLT: Local Encoders, a Global Transformer, and Cross-Attention
blogs.description: A friendly tour of BLT’s three-part design: lightweight byte-level encoder and decoder wrapped around a larger global latent transformer. Show how cross-attention pools bytes into patches and back, why most compute runs at the patch level, and how this architecture saves FLOPs.

blogs.title: Do Patches Scale Better Than Tokens? What the Scaling Curves Show
blogs.description: Turn the paper’s scaling studies into clear takeaways. Cover flop-controlled parity with token models up to 8B parameters, fixed-inference scaling where bigger patches let the global model grow, and why patch sizes around 6–8 bytes can deliver large inference savings at scale.

blogs.title: Built for the Long Tail: BLT’s Robustness to Typos, Noise, and Low-Resource Languages
blogs.description: Summarize BLT’s wins on character-level tasks (like CUTE and G2P), noise-robust evaluations, and low-resource translation benchmarks. Explain in simple terms why byte-level modeling sees and manipulates subword structure that token-based models often miss.

blogs.title: The Patch Size Playbook: How to Trade Speed and Accuracy with BLT
blogs.description: Offer practical guidance on choosing average patch size and entropy thresholds. Explain how keeping total context bytes constant avoids unfair comparisons, why larger patches reduce inference steps, and when to lower the entropy threshold at inference to boost accuracy on hard tasks.

blogs.title: From Llama to BLT: Byte-ifying a Tokenized Model
blogs.description: Walk through the paper’s recipe for initializing BLT from a pre-trained Llama 3.1: reuse the global transformer, train lightweight local modules, and lightly finetune. Share the gains, current gaps, and what this means for teams that want tokenizer-free models without full retraining.

blogs.title: Tokenization’s Hidden Costs: Bias, Brittleness, and a Bigger Softmax
blogs.description: Explain why fixed vocabularies can be a bottleneck: domain sensitivity, multilingual inequity, brittleness to spelling and noise, and the compute tradeoff of large vocabularies. Show how BLT removes the vocabulary and reallocates compute exactly where data is complex.
